text:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 decode latency breach detected in prod-eu-west-1 (model: r-gen-2). p99 = 3.6s (> SLO 1.5s) observed across streaming endpoints. Triggered 5m ago. Paging indicators: kernel page-fault rate ↑, decode stalls, KV cache miss spike. Auto-mitigation: none. Runbook: /runbooks/decode-latency.
oncall-alex: seeing the same on Grafana. p95 also creeping up to ~700ms. Streaming sessions dropping frames, some client disconnects.
runtime-joe: recent kernel build? We rolled kernel-retune v4.12.7 last night to eu-west nodes for flashattn/TF integration.
oncall-alex: yes, cluster-tag euw-kernel-4-12 pushed 02:14Z. Rolling back would be fastest mitigation but need coord with infra.
infra-liz: confirming: kernel-retune v4.12.7 staged to euw pool (batch of 40 nodes). Canary looked ok but we didn't run long-tail streaming profile.
sre-maya: can we confirm paging counters on affected hosts? Sharing quick command: 
```
ssh jump@euw-n1 sudo perf stat -e page-faults,minor-faults -p $(pgrep runtime) -- sleep 10
```
runtime-joe: pasted sample from one host: 
```
# host euw-n1
page-faults:  124520
minor-faults: 124480
# decode logs: kv_cache_miss=0.32 tail_latency_ms=3820 active_streams=113
```
infra-liz: that page-faults number looks high vs baseline (baseline ~2k). Looks like an ABI change in kernel affecting mmap/hugepage behavior.
cs-raul: customer impact: two enterprise customers flagged increased 502s from streaming endpoints (~1.8% -> 7.4%). They're on Dedicated tenants in eu-west. Raising their severity to P1.
eng-ops: any recent compiler or TRT/FlashAttention changes in runtime?
runtime-joe: we merged a FlashAttention ABI shim and a compiler flag -march=nvptx64-retune in the decode pipeline a week ago. Suspect mismatch with the kernel's page alignment changes.
oncall-alex: immediate remediation options: 1) Rollback kernel-retune v4.12.7 on the affected euw pool (requires infra deploy and careful node drain) 2) Evacuate traffic from eu-west to eu-central fallback pool (application-level routing) 3) Enable software fallback path in runtime to disable flashattn kernels (hot flag) 4) Patch hugepage/mmap settings on hosts (sysctl) to reduce page faults.
sre-maya: ordering by speed: enable hot flag in runtime (3) is fastest (~2-3m), route traffic (2) next (requires load-balancer update), rollback kernel (1) takes longer (~20-40m with safe drains).
runtime-joe: I can flip hot flag: `REDWOOD_RUNTIME_DISABLE_FLASHATTN=1` via staging config toggle in config-service. Will do canary on 5 nodes then blast.
oncall-alex: do it. Start with 5 nodes, monitor p99. Set notify on p99 drop below 1.6s.
runtime-joe: rolling now -> canary started on node ids [euw-n1,euw-n3,euw-n7,euw-n12,euw-n20].
incident-bot: NOTE: config change recorded by ops-audit (chg_98321).
runtime-joe: canary p99 down to 1.4s on those nodes after flag. KV cache miss rate also dropped to 0.08.
oncall-alex: good. Start blast to remaining euw nodes.
infra-liz: rebalancer: switching 80% of new sessions to eu-central while roll completes, should reduce customer impact for dedicated tenants.
cs-raul: update from customer A: seeing improvement on new sessions, but old sessions still experience disconnects. They're asking for ETA on full resolution.
sre-maya: action items: - runtime to finish hot-flag blast and monitor (owner: runtime-joe) - infra to prepare safe rollback plan for kernel-retune v4.12.7 in case metrics regress (owner: infra-liz) - eng-ops to collect perf traces and send to kernel team (owner: eng-ops) - cs to notify affected customers and collect logs (owner: cs-raul).
eng-ops: grabbing perf trace: `sudo perf record -F 99 -a -g -- sleep 30` then `perf report`. Uploading to /tmp/retune-traces.tar.gz -> link: https://internal.redwood/trace/retune-traces.tar.gz
runtime-joe: blast completed. euw cluster p99 now 1.2s, p95 320ms. Streaming disconnects reduced ~90%.
oncall-alex: big +1. Keep monitoring for 30m. If stable, we can keep hot flag while kernel team investigates real fix.
infra-liz: started rollback runbook prep in case we need to revert kernel staging, documenting nodes and service windows. ETA 35m to be ready.
eng-ops: initial perf report attached: top symbols show spike in copy_user and do_page_fault paths when flashattn kernel used. Suspect the new kernel changed page alignment/hugemode handling.
sre-maya: escalate to kernel infra team and cc: @kernel-team. Can we get a quick patch suggestion?
eng-ops: sending the trace + diff to kernel-team. Quick workaround: set `vm.max_map_count` and tune `vm.nr_hugepages` to increase hugepage allocations, but this is host-level and not ideal.
cs-raul: customers A and B updated. They want 1) confirmation of mitigation, 2) root cause timeline, 3) follow-up postmortem.
oncall-alex: agreed — we'll prepare incident timeline and RCA. For now maintain hot-flag and traffic steering.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: p99 reduced to 1.2s in eu-west after mitigation. SLA impact reduced. Continue monitoring.
eng-ops: starting a short-term debounce script to clear KV cache cold starts for affected models: `python tools/kv_warmer.py --model r-gen-2 --nodes euw-*` to smooth tail.
runtime-joe: warming started. Expect further p99 gains over 15-30m.
infra-liz: kernel-team replied in thread: "looking at ABI mismatch, will test small repro on kernel-retune branch. If confirmed, we will push a micro-patch to restore previous mmap flags." Kernel-team asked for exact config: we provided `/proc/sys/vm/nr_hugepages` and mount flags.
sre-maya: oncall handoff plan: I'll follow for next 2 hours and then hand off to infra-liz for persistent remediation tracking. Update timeline: 30m for stability check, 2-4h for full rollback or patch.
oncall-alex: handing off now to SRE: @sre-maya takes lead. Please summarize status in incidents channel and file initial incident doc.
sre-maya: ACK. Summary: mitigation applied (flashattn disabled via hot flag), p99 back to SLO-ish, customers notified (CS). Next: kernel patch verification and long-term mitigation (rollback or kernel micro-patch). I'll create incident ticket and link.
cs-raul: logging customer request for postmortem; collecting logs and timelines now.
oncall-alex: thanks everyone. If anything regresses ping here and escalate to P0. React :white_check_mark: when you have your action item done.
eng-ops: ✅ perf traces uploaded.
runtime-joe: ✅ hot-flag blast completed.
infra-liz: ✅ rollback plan draft created: https://internal.redwood/doc/euw-kernel-rollback-draft
sre-maya: ✅ handoff noted. I'll open the incident in Jira and tag kernel-team, runtime, infra, CS.
incident-bot: RESOLVE CHECKPOINT: If metrics remain stable for 30m, mark incident as mitigated and move to postmortem.
oncall-alex: marking thread for watch.
